steps.title: Three levels
steps.body: The defense has 11 too, stacked in ==three levels==: the line up front, linebackers behind them, and the ==secondary== deep.

steps.title: Defensive line
steps.body: Tackles in the middle, ends on the edges. They ==rush the passer== and ==plug running lanes==. Tackle the QB behind the line and it's a sack.

steps.title: Linebackers
steps.body: The do-everything level: ==tackle runners==, cover short passes, ==blitz== the QB. The middle linebacker usually calls the defense's play.
steps.note: He's often called the quarterback of the defense.

steps.title: Cornerbacks
steps.body: Corners line up across from the wide receivers and ==shadow them== on every route. Their job is to break up passes, or ==pick them off==.

steps.title: Safeties
steps.body: The deepest players on the field. Safeties stop the long pass and make the tackle when everyone else misses. They're the ==last line of defense==.

steps.title: The blitz
steps.body: A blitz sends ==extra rushers==, usually linebackers or a safety, at the QB. It can force a quick sack, but it leaves ==fewer players in coverage==.

steps.explain: He started at the second level, behind the line, then shot through the gap. That's a linebacker blitz.

steps.prompt: Who is the last line of defense against a deep pass?
steps.explain: Safeties play deepest. If a receiver gets behind everyone else, they're the ones left to stop him.
